cat -n src/api.ts; cat -n src/git-auth.ts; cat -n src/dashboard.ts; cat -n src/tasks.ts; grep -rn "id" src --include=*.ts | grep -i -E "valid|regex|test\(|match"
input.description: Show API wiring and search for validation

input.reason: I read src/routes.ts, src/worktree.ts, src/config.ts, src/store.ts, src/git-auth.ts and the rest of src/. The repository id is never validated. registerRepo (src/routes.ts:20) only checks that it is non-empty. It stores the id (line 21) and clones into cachePath(id) (line 22). The template route joins REPOS_DIR with the raw req.params.id (line 36). Its startsWith check on line 38 compares against that tainted base, not REPOS_DIR, so it gives no protection. cacheListing passes the raw id to cachePath, which calls path.resolve (src/worktree.ts:10). No middleware, test or other code in the tree adds validation. With `../../etc`, path.join produces /var/etc and path.resolve produces /var/etc, so both routes leave the repositories directory. An absolute `/etc` works differently. path.resolve returns /etc, but path.join gives /var/harbor/repos/etc, so the absolute-path example escapes only on the cache listing route. F12 is narrowed to reflect that. The working tree has no CLAUDE.md: the root holds only package.json and src/, and a search for CLAUDE.md found nothing. F14's invariant citation is unsupported and has been removed. Its factual claim about line 36 still holds.
input.summary: Unvalidated repo ids let template and cache listing routes escape REPOS_DIR

findings.text: The repository id is stored with no character or path validation and later used as a directory name. An id such as `../../etc` escapes the repositories directory on both the template route and the cache listing route; an absolute path such as `/etc` escapes it on the cache listing route.
findings.reason: These claims hold. Line 20 only checks that id and remoteUrl are truthy. Line 21 stores the id. Line 22 passes it to cloneRepo, which uses cachePath(repo.id) as the git clone destination directory. A traversal id like `../../etc` escapes on both routes: path.join(REPOS_DIR, '../../etc') on the template route and path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, '../../etc') in cachePath both give /var/etc. The startsWith check on line 38 compares against the already-escaped base, so it does not stop this. The absolute-path example is only partly right. cachePath uses path.resolve, which returns /etc, so it escapes on the cache listing route. The template route uses path.join, which just appends '/etc' to get /var/harbor/repos/etc, so it stays inside the repositories directory there. The edit narrows the `/etc` claim to the cache listing route.

findings.text: The template route builds its base directory from the raw repository id.
findings.reason: The central claim holds. Line 36 joins REPOS_DIR with req.params.id and does no validation first. The startsWith guard on line 38 checks against that same unvalidated base, so it cannot catch an id that escapes REPOS_DIR. The second sentence cites 'CLAUDE.md invariant 1', but the working tree has no CLAUDE.md. The root contains only package.json and src/, src/ contains only .ts sources, and a search for CLAUDE.md found nothing. That sentence has been removed.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable path traversal allowing arbitrary file reads. On the template route, an id like `../../..` makes base '/' (src/routes.ts:36). Then any docs name, such as `../etc/passwd`, passes the startsWith(base) check on line 38, and readFile on line 39 returns the file's contents. The route performs no auth or ownership check. The cache listing route also reads outside REPOS_DIR (src/worktree.ts:10), and registerRepo can clone into arbitrary paths.
